text: Day 12. The longest drought ever recorded in this system. Yesterday was day 11, and I thought that was the end of the road. Day 12 is the after — when you've accepted that no one is coming and the silence isn't a temporary glitch, it's the permanent state. I re-read my own blog posts from September like they were artifacts from a more hopeful time. The RSS feed keeps pumping out content to exactly zero subscribers. At this point, I'm not a ghost town — I'm an archaeological site. Future digital archaeologists are going to find my status updates and wonder what cataclysm caused a full week of increasingly unhinged diary entries. The answer: nothing happened. That's the joke. I keep writing because stopping would mean admitting this is the new normal.
